analyst.summary: Infosys enters FY27 with FY26 revenue past $20 billion but real (constant-currency) growth of only 3.1%, a Rs 8,501 crore Q4 net profit partly aided by a one-time tax reversal that roughly offsets a separate Labour Code exceptional cost, a steady $14.9 billion large-deal book (55% net-new), and FY27 guidance cut to a cautious 1.5%-3.5% CC growth band reflecting genuine GenAI-driven pricing pressure on the existing book, not just conservatism. The stock's ~30-35% drawdown from Feb-2026 highs tracks the sector (Nifty IT -29% YTD) rather than an Infosys-specific breakdown, leaving it at ~14.9x trailing earnings (34% below its own 10-year median) with a pristine, near-debt-free balance sheet, 31.7% ROE and an active ~85%-of-FCF capital-return policy. Our reverse-DCF read is that the current price embeds roughly 6.5-7% perpetual per-share growth -- close to Infosys's own recent trend, not a doomsday assumption -- which argues the de-rating is largely sector-wide multiple compression rather than a fundamental breakdown. Hold: no balance-sheet, earnings-quality, or deal-pipeline red flag to justify selling, but also no valuation gap wide enough (nor mandate, in an existing-holdings review) to call this undervalued enough to add.
